title: Implement the supplied interval sampler with fixed fair-bit blocks while retaining D_G depth
statement: For every fixed positive rational lambda=a/b, the source's finite-word implementation of the supplied Miao-Yin random-scan interval sampler uses N=O_lambda(mL^2) updates, each specified by two k-bit integers with k=ceil(log2(8N(m+1)/epsilon)). Edge floor-rounding and a finite Bernoulli threshold give total instruction-law error <=epsilon/8 with 2Nk=O_lambda(mL^3) charged fair bits. Under the imported record-work and tail bounds, cap interval rounds at overflow probability epsilon/4 and output the empty matching on overflow; reference mixing error epsilon/4 plus those errors is <epsilon. The source claims worst-case W_bit<=C_lambda(n+m+B)L^c and D_PRAM<=C_lambda(1+D_G)L^c, where D_G=min{Delta,ceil(m^(1/3)),ceil(sqrt(n))} for m>=1; m=0 is deterministic empty output. This is a restricted sublinear-depth implementation argument, not the requested all-degree polylog-depth sampler.

The finite-word proposition is the source's implementation argument under the supplied Miao-Yin theorem/record-work contracts; it is not a new Capital proof audit or executed implementation. costs: Under the explicitly supplied Miao-Yin mixing, interval-record and record-charged-work bounds, N=ceil(C_lambda*m*(log^2(n+2)+log(4/epsilon)))=O_lambda(mL^2) updates suffice for reference mixing error epsilon/4. Set p=a/(a+b) for lambda=a/b and k=ceil(log2(8N(m+1)/epsilon)). Each instruction uses two k-bit uniform integers: edge 1+floor(mU/2^k), coin indicator{V<floor(p*2^k)}. Their full instruction-law error is <=N(m+1)/2^k<=epsilon/8, using 2Nk=O_lambda(mL^3) charged bits and finite integer arithmetic. Apply the imported interval-simulation tail bound with overflow budget epsilon/4 and a deterministic round cap; overflow outputs a valid empty matching. Mixing+bit+overflow error is <epsilon. The source claims worst-case bit work C_lambda(n+m+B)L^c and depth C_lambda(1+D_G)L^c; Capital does not newly verify those imported record/scheduling bounds or execute this algorithm.
